sections.html:
Wright County is a rural county in north central Iowa with Clarion as its county seat and Eagle Grove as its largest city. It covers 582 square miles, of which 580 are land, and the terrain is generally undulating.

The Boone and Iowa rivers cross the county. Neighbors are Hancock to the north, Cerro Gordo to the northeast, Franklin to the east, Hardin to the southeast, Hamilton to the south, Webster to the southwest, Humboldt to the west and Kossuth to the northwest.

The county was organized in January 1851, effective January 15. It is named for either Silas Wright, a New York governor, or Joseph Albert Wright, an Indiana governor, and sources do not settle which.

sections.h2: How many people live in Wright County?
sections.html:
Wright County had 12,943 residents in the 2020 census, about 22 people per square mile, and an estimated 12,801 in 2025. The median age is 41.0.

sections.h2: What do Census Bureau numbers show for Wright County housing?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau reports a median value of $109,800 for owner-occupied homes in Wright County for 2019 to 2023, with 74.2 percent of homes owner-occupied. The county had 6,276 housing units in 2023.

  • Median gross rent: $788
  • Median household income: $64,033
  • Persons per household: 2.36
  • Bachelor's degree or higher, age 25+: 23.5%
  • Mean travel time to work: 19.2 minutes

Those are county medians, so a repair estimate that looks small in a larger market can matter more here when a median home is valued near $110,000.

sections.h2: How did Clarion become the county seat?
sections.html:
Clarion became the county seat in 1866 after the seat had been at Liberty since 1858. Wright County held its first court sessions in 1855 in a log cabin west of present-day Eagle Grove.

The present courthouse was built in 1891 and 1892 for about $50,000 and was added to the National Register of Historic Places in 1981. Clarion had 2,810 residents in 2020, down from 2,968 in 2000.

Clarion's July average high is 85.0 degrees F and its January average high is 25.8 degrees F. Annual precipitation averages 34.27 inches, with 31.1 inches of snow, and the record low is minus 32 degrees F.

Employers named in local sources lean toward food production and farm equipment. Clarion has a 114,000 square foot egg carton plant, Clarion Packaging, and Hagie Manufacturing, which builds high-clearance sprayers.

  • Prestage Foods of Iowa, a pork plant near Eagle Grove, had hired about 500 people by 2019, and a 2019 report said it spurred a housing construction boom in Eagle Grove and nearby towns.
  • The county bought 80 acres for an Agribusiness Park near Iowa Highway 17, 320th Street and the Prestage plant, and Ennis Corp. opened a washout business there in March 2021.
  • Iowa Specialty Hospital in Clarion employs about 450 people and serves a 75-mile radius.

Clarion won approval for an $8.1 million low-interest USDA loan to build a new water treatment plant, and Eagle Grove has opened a housing district on its southeast side with lots for sale.

sections.h2: Which school districts serve Wright County?
sections.html:
Wright County has six active school districts, including Clarion-Goldfield-Dows, Eagle Grove and Belmond-Klemme. Several older districts merged or dissolved over the years.

Clarion-Goldfield-Dows took its current form when Dows joined on July 1, 2014. The Eagle Grove district serves about 836 students across Wright, Humboldt and Webster counties. Iowa Central Community College in Fort Dodge, North Iowa Area Community College in Mason City and Ellsworth Community College in Iowa Falls are the nearest community colleges.

sections.h2: Which Wright County offices handle property tax?
sections.html:
The county offices are in the Wright County Courthouse at 115 North Main Street in Clarion. The courthouse is open Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 4 p.m., and the main line is (515) 851-0202.

  • Treasurer: 515-532-2691, PO Box 226. Peggy Schluttenhofer is listed in the 2026 tax sale notice.
  • Assessor: 515-532-3737, PO Box 428, listed under Tonee Nicholas.
  • Recorder: 515-532-3204, PO Box 187, listed under Eric Russell.
  • Auditor: 515-532-2771, listed under Amanda Meyer.

Taxes can be paid online through iowatreasurers.org. Property records are on the county's Beacon site.

sections.h2: What credits and reviews does the Wright County Assessor handle?
sections.html:
The assessor takes homestead applications on Form 54-028, due July 1. A homeowner who is 65 or older by January 1 of the assessment year can also claim an exemption created by House File 718, signed May 4, 2023.

That exemption reduces taxable value by $3,250 for 2023 assessments and $6,500 for assessment years beginning January 1, 2024 or later. Once granted it continues without refiling, as long as the owner still qualifies.

Two data collectors visit properties and leave a door tag, either "no action necessary" or "please contact our office." They started on all of Clarion on May 19, 2026, the first review there since 2019, after covering Lake Cornelia and then Elm Lake from July 23, 2025.

Iowa sets the Board of Review window for protests at April 2 through April 30 under Iowa Code 441.37. Confirm the assessment year and any county notice with the assessor at 515-532-3737.

sections.h2: When are Wright County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Iowa property taxes are due in two halves on September 1 and March 1, and late interest of 1.5 percent a month is added on October 1 and April 1. In a normal sale, taxes are prorated at closing and the buyer is credited for the seller's portion.

Transfers carry Iowa's real estate transfer tax of 80 cents for each $500 of value above the first $500. The seller is liable under Iowa Code 428A.3, and the recorder will not record a taxable deed until it is paid.

sections.h2: How does the Wright County tax sale work?
sections.html:
Wright County scheduled its 2026 tax sale for Monday, June 15, 2026, with bidding from 9:00 a.m. to 11:00 a.m. The courthouse hosts the sale, and bids are placed online at iowataxauction.com. The list of parcels was published in the Wright County Independent in Belmond.

  • Redemption interest is 2 percent per month on the amount paid, counting each part of a month as a whole month.
  • A 90-day notice of right of redemption may be issued after 1 year and 9 months for a regular sale, or 9 months for a public bidder sale.
  • Certificate fee: $20. Treasurer's deed fee: $25 per parcel.
  • A certificate is canceled if no affidavit of service is filed within three years of the sale.

An owner of a parcel that has been sold should get a payoff figure from the treasurer before arranging a sale.

sections.h2: What should a Wright County owner consider before selling?
sections.html:
With a county median value of $109,800, buyers in Clarion, Eagle Grove or Belmond often weigh repair costs closely against the price. A house that needs work may be easier to sell as-is than to renovate first.

We buy Wright County houses as-is, including those with delinquent taxes. Send us the address and the latest tax statement, and we will reply with a written offer.

faqs.q: What is the county seat of Wright County, Iowa?
faqs.a: Clarion is the county seat. The county courthouse is at 115 North Main Street, and Eagle Grove is the largest city.

faqs.q: When is the homestead credit deadline in Wright County?
faqs.a: Homestead applications are due July 1 to the Wright County Assessor on Form 54-028. Owners 65 or older may also qualify for a separate exemption under House File 718.

faqs.q: How do I pay Wright County property tax?
faqs.a: Pay online at iowatreasurers.org or contact the treasurer at 515-532-2691. Taxes are due September 1 and March 1, with late interest of 1.5 percent a month.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to redeem property sold at the Wright County tax sale?
faqs.a: The owner pays the amount sold plus 2 percent a month, counting each part of a month as a whole month, and the $20 certificate fee. Ask the treasurer for an exact payoff.

faqs.q: Which Wright County town has the most people?
faqs.a: Eagle Grove, with 3,601 residents in 2020. Clarion followed with 2,810 and Belmond with 2,463.
